findings.summary: The frozen I0, I1, W0, D0, and independently prepared P0 controls all executed under the compilation-plus-semantic contract. Ambient, pinned, and governed webgpu@0.3.0 fail; Doe and the bounded webgpu@0.3.10 plus no-isolation control both complete all 13 assertions, the 110-function compilation corpus, exact smoothStep dispatch/readback, and replay.

The independently prepared webgpu@0.3.10 package executes the exact semantic oracle but intermittently corrupts Node test-worker IPC. Node's explicit no-isolation mode removes that wrapper-level failure without changing the tests, shaders, GPU work, diagnostics, or oracle; P0 passes every clean process and replay.

D0 remains a correct and stable implementation, but it does not materially exceed the bounded P0 control on the exercised application outcome. The runtime-ownership hypothesis is rejected for wgsl-fns at this scope.

limitations: The semantic oracle executes one upstream function exactly; the other generated functions remain compilation-only and cannot inherit semantic coverage.
P0 uses a different Node process topology; it closes the exercised outcome but does not prove that no-isolation mode is acceptable for every downstream CI policy.
The P0 package has an independent registry-integrity and artifact-hash receipt, but the upstream application checkout was reused rather than freshly installed inside this diagnostic run.
The incumbent probe aborts before complete adapter identity, so no performance comparison is admissible.
Three clean processes are diagnostic and below the promotion reliability floor.
The result rejects DoeRuntime ownership for this application and does not create a release blocker.

performance.reason: D0 and P0 execute equivalent GPU work through different Node test-isolation topologies, so their process durations are diagnostic rather than a fair runtime comparison.

receiptOverhead.reason: Matched traced and untraced receipt-overhead samples were not collected.

I0.summary: Ordinary workspace resolution selects webgpu@0.3.0 and aborts before the complete corpus.

I1.summary: Explicitly pinned webgpu@0.3.0 reproduces the native worker crash.

W0.summary: DoeProof reproduces and explains the pinned failure but cannot correct it above the incumbent runtime boundary.

D0.summary: DoeRuntime passes the full compilation corpus, exact semantic dispatch/readback, physical provider check, and receipt replay.

P0.summary: The independently prepared webgpu@0.3.10 package plus explicit no-isolation test mode passes the full corpus, exact semantic dispatch/readback, physical provider check, and replay.

materialOutcome.summary: D0 does not materially exceed P0 on the frozen correctness, semantic execution, diagnostics, reliability, or replay outcome.

costAcceptance.summary: No unique application benefit was measured to repay DoeRuntime's additional source, compatibility, security, packaging, and support obligations.

installation.summary: The P0 package has independent registry and artifact closure, but the upstream checkout was reused and no clean-install application receipt was produced for this run.

supportHardware.summary: Doe and P0 probe the physical AMD Vulkan host, but ambient and pinned incumbents abort before complete adapter identity.

concurrency.summary: The matrix uses sequential clean processes.

teardown.summary: Successful Doe processes clean up, but promotion-scale teardown cycles were not run.

stress.summary: No promotion-scale stress contract was run.

memory.summary: Peak memory was recorded without bounded-growth testing.

receipts.summary: The raw matrix, provider summary, and W0, D0, and P0 replay inputs are hash-bound.

replay.summary: W0, D0, and the bounded P0 construction reproduce their complete evidence.

performance.summary: D0 and P0 process timings are not comparable because P0 intentionally changes Node test isolation.

ownership.summary: The matrix is complete, but D0 supplies no measured application advantage over the bounded P0 correction.

release.summary: wgsl-fns remains diagnostic and does not block Doe releases.
